name: htmlradar-mcp

tools.name: share_html
tools.description: Publishes an HTML document (a deck, report, dashboard, proposal or one-pager) as a tracked HTMLRadar link, and returns two addresses: the link for the recipient, and a dashboard address for the sender. The recipient sees the document as written and never the tracking. The markup goes in `html`; there is no file-path argument, so a file on disk is published by passing its markup. By default the recipient is asked for their email address before the document opens. The new HTML is screened for phishing signals as every upload is; the link is live the moment it is returned unless the screen holds the page, and readers of a held page see that it is not available yet. The answer includes the saved rules and whether comments are on. The document id that create_share and replace_document take comes from list_documents or list_shares. Markup is limited to 5 MB. Images that need a login, expiring image addresses and local file paths do not load for readers of the link; an image embedded in the HTML as a data URI travels inside the page. The tool does not check that images load.

html.description: The HTML markup to publish, in full. There is no file-path argument: a document on disk reaches this tool only as markup the caller has already read.

title.description: The document's name on your dashboard. Readers can see it too: it names the page in the one-time code email they receive.

comments.description: Whether readers can comment. Off by default. Turning comments on needs the email gate and a one-time code; who sees comments follows the link.

recipient_label.description: Who this link is for. A separate link for each recipient separates their reading reports.

require_email.description: Whether the recipient must give an email address before the document opens. Defaults to true.

verify_email.description: Whether the reader must prove their email address with a six-digit code before the document opens. Off by default. A verified address identifies the reader rather than an address merely typed into the gate. Needs the email gate, which is on by default; with it off the call is refused.

password.description: Extra password gate on top of the email gate.

lock_deck.description: Blocks save and print; default true. False allows a recipient to keep a copy.

show_watermark.description: Show a faint watermark when lock_deck is true. Defaults to true on creation; omitted on edit keeps the saved choice.

allowed_email_domains.description: Only these email domains may open the link, e.g. ["acme.com"]. Up to 500. Needs the email gate, which is on by default; with it off the call is refused.

allowed_emails.description: Only these exact addresses may open the link. A separate list from the domains, and a visitor passes on either. Up to 500 addresses; an allowed domain covers all addresses in that domain. Needs the email gate, which is on by default; with it off the call is refused.

expires_in_hours.description: Link stops working after this many hours.

slug.description: Custom link name, so the URL reads /r/acme-proposal. Paid plans only.

request_id.description: Optional on a first attempt. When a previous call may have been applied, the request_id named by its error makes a retry return the first result instead of doing it twice.

tools.name: create_share
tools.description: Creates an additional tracked link for a document already on HTMLRadar, with its own recipient label, gate, password, expiry and address. One link per recipient is what separates their reading reports. It uploads nothing and creates no second copy of the document, and it cannot publish new markup. The document id comes from list_documents or list_shares. The link is live the moment it is returned, but a held or blocked document does not open for readers through any link. The answer includes the saved rules and whether comments are on.

document_id.description: The document to make another link for: the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

tools.name: list_shares
tools.description: Lists the account's tracked links, newest first: the slug, the recipient label, the document title, whether it has been opened and when, and the share and document ids for each link. A link made in an earlier conversation is found here. The `opened` and `last_open` fields show which links nobody has opened. Returns at most 50 per call; the `before` cursor pages back through older links.

before.description: Cursor for the next page: the `next_before` value printed at the end of a previous list_shares result, of the form <created_at>|<share id>. Its exact value selects the next page; omission selects the most recent links.

annotations.title: List tracked links on this account

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: Lists the account's documents, newest first: the title, when it was created, how many tracked links point at it, and its document id. A document with no links appears here and not in list_shares, which lists only documents that have been sent. It returns no document contents. Returns at most 50 per call; the `before` cursor pages back through older documents.

before.description: Cursor for the next page: the `next_before` value printed at the end of a previous list_documents result, of the form <created_at>|<document id>. Its exact value selects the next page; omission selects the most recent documents.

tools.name: get_share_activity
tools.description: Reports whether a tracked HTMLRadar link has been opened and how many read it. For each reader shown in full, it reports who they are, how long they read, how far they scrolled, and all recorded sections ordered by reading time. On Free, the first five readers of a link are shown in full; later readers appear as a "more read it" count. Reading times are rounded down; scroll percentages are rounded to the nearest whole percent. It accepts the link's share id, slug or full address. With `include_detail`, each reader shown in full has their country, city, device and referring page added.

share_id.description: The share id returned by share_html, or the share's slug (the part after /r/ in its link), or the link itself.

include_detail.description: Also return each reader's country, city, device and referrer. Off by default; whether the document was read, and which parts, is answered without it.

annotations.title: Check who read a tracked link

tools.name: revoke_share
tools.description: Switches off a tracked link that has already been sent. Anyone who opens it afterwards sees that it is no longer available, and the sender is emailed that somebody tried, at most once every six hours for a link. This changes what a recipient can see. It is reversible: `revoked: false` switches a link back on, however long ago it was switched off, but a link past its end date stays closed until update_share sets a new end date or clears it. It deletes nothing: the link, its settings and its whole reading history survive. Deleting a link is possible only on the website, because it deletes its reading records for good. update_share changes a link's settings without changing its address; switching one off to make a replacement leaves the recipient holding a dead address.

share_id.description: The link's share id, slug (the part after /r/), or full address.

revoked.description: True (the default) switches the link off. False switches it back on.

annotations.title: Switch a tracked link off, or back on

tools.name: get_share
tools.description: Returns a tracked link's current settings, in the form update_share changes them: who can open it (the full allowed-domain and allowed-address lists), the email gate and its one-time code, whether a password is set (never the password), the end date, the copy lock, comments, the label, who the gate names, whether the sender is emailed on the first open, and the settings version. It reads one of this account's links and changes nothing. The answer includes the saved rules and the settings version that update_share takes as expected_settings_version.

share_id.description: The link's share id, slug (the part after /r/), or full address.

tools.name: update_share
tools.description: Changes the settings of a tracked link that has already been sent, on the same link: who can open it (allowed domains and addresses), the email gate and its one-time code, the password, the end date, the copy lock, the label, who the gate names and whether the sender is emailed on the first open. Comments can be on or off; enabling needs a code-confirmed email gate. The answer includes the saved rules. The link, its address and its whole reading history stay the same. Only the settings named in the call change; every other setting is left as it is, and a setting is removed when it is named in `clear` (a recipient_label of only spaces also removes the label). The list arguments add_allowed_emails, remove_allowed_emails, add_allowed_email_domains and remove_allowed_email_domains: the server merges them over the stored list and says what was added, removed and not found. Replacing or clearing a whole list (sending allowed_emails or allowed_email_domains, or naming one in `clear`) needs expected_settings_version, the settings version get_share returned, so a change made since is never overwritten. A stale version is refused without saving. A change applies from the next time the page is loaded: someone reading it right now keeps the page they have until they reload. If the sender is on a company team, the team's rules apply to this change exactly as on the website (for example a required one-time code or company domains), and a change that breaks one is refused with the rule named. Narrowing who can open a link, or removing a list, changes what recipients can see.

comments.description: Whether readers can comment. Omitted keeps the current choice. Turning comments on needs the email gate and a one-time code; who sees comments follows the link.

share_id.description: The link's share id, slug (the part after /r/), or full address.

recipient_label.description: A new label for who this link is for, e.g. "Acme".

require_email.description: Whether the email gate is on. Turning it off removes the check that the list of allowed domains and addresses relies on; those lists must be cleared in the same call.

verify_email.description: Whether the one-time-code check is on: the reader receives a six-digit code and opens the document only when they type it back. Needs the email gate on.

password.description: A password of at least 8 characters on top of the email gate. `clear` removes it.

lock_deck.description: The copy lock: true blocks save and print; false allows them.

show_watermark.description: Show a faint watermark when lock_deck is true. Defaults to true on creation; omitted on edit keeps the saved choice.

allowed_email_domains.description: Only these email domains may open the link, e.g. ["acme.com"]. This REPLACES the whole stored list, so entries absent from this value are removed. `clear` removes the list. Needs the email gate on.

allowed_emails.description: Only these exact addresses may open the link. A separate list from the domains; a visitor passes on either. This REPLACES the whole stored list, so entries absent from this value are removed. `clear` removes the list. Needs the email gate on.

add_allowed_emails.description: Addresses to ADD to the stored list of allowed addresses. The server merges them over the list as it is now, so nothing has to be copied back. Needs the email gate on.

remove_allowed_emails.description: Addresses to REMOVE from the stored list of allowed addresses. The answer says which were not on the list. Removing the last entry of every list is refused; `clear` removes a whole list.

add_allowed_email_domains.description: Domains to ADD to the stored list of allowed domains, merged on the server.

remove_allowed_email_domains.description: Domains to REMOVE from the stored list of allowed domains, merged on the server.

expected_settings_version.description: The settings version get_share showed. The change is made only if the link is still at that version; if the settings changed since they were read, nothing is changed and the call returns the current settings version. Required when a whole allowed-address or allowed-domain list is replaced or cleared.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, as a date and time such as 2026-12-31T17:00:00Z. Mutually exclusive with `expires_in_hours`. `clear` removes the end date.

expires_in_hours.description: The link stops working this many hours from now. Mutually exclusive with `expires_at`.

show_sender.description: Who the gate names to the reader: nobody, the sender's company, or the sender's name. The company needs a work sign-up address; the name needs one set in Settings.

notify_first_open.description: Whether the sender is e-mailed when someone reads this link.

clear.description: Settings to remove: the label, the password, the end date, the domain list, the address list. Removing a list lets anyone who passes the email gate in. A setting that is not named here or above is left exactly as it is.

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.description: Lists the files attached to a document on HTMLRadar (supporting materials a reader can download beside the page): the file name, its size and the attachment id. It returns no file contents and changes nothing. After an add_attachment call that gave no answer, this list shows whether the file was attached.

document_id.description: The document: the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

tools.name: add_attachment
tools.description: Attaches one file to a document already on HTMLRadar, for readers of its links to download. The file types are the website's (PDF, Office documents, images, CSV, text, Markdown, ZIP) and a document holds up to 20 files. The file travels as base64 in `content_base64`, because a tool argument is JSON, so it can be at most 5.0 MB, the same limit as publishing a page this way; a larger file (the website takes 25 MB) is added on the website. Readers see the file from the next time they load the page. There is no file-path argument.

document_id.description: The document: the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

filename.description: The file name with its extension, e.g. "pricing.pdf". The extension decides the type.

annotations.title: Attach a file to a document

tools.name: remove_attachment
tools.description: Removes one attached file from a document. Downloads stop at once, even from a page a reader already has open; the file leaves the page's list the next time the page loads. Copies a reader already downloaded stay with them. It removes the file only: the page, its links and its reading history are untouched, and there is no tool that deletes a page or a link. The file cannot be recovered from HTMLRadar; attaching it again needs the original file. list_attachments returns the attachment id.

document_id.description: The document the file is attached to: from list_documents or list_shares.

annotations.title: Remove a file from a document

tools.name: get_reading_records
tools.description: Returns the reading records the HTMLRadar website exports as a spreadsheet, as CSV text: for readers shown in full, one row per section per read (a read with no section recorded has one row with the section columns blank; section_status says "not measured" when the page changed while it was being read, so no section time was taken), with the link's label and slug, the reader, whether their address was verified, when they opened it, how long they read, how far they scrolled, and their country and device where recorded. On Free, the first five readers of a link are shown in full; later readers appear in a "more read it" count row without their individual details. The sender's own previews and internal viewers are left out, as on the website. With `share_id`, the records cover one link; without it every link of the document is included. A very long answer is cut at a whole record and gives a `continue_from` value for the remaining rows. The website file itself holds only the oldest 5,000 reads of a document or link, and the result says when it is every row of that file and when the file is capped. It changes nothing. It is the full export; get_share_activity summarises one link.

document_id.description: The document: the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

share_id.description: Limit the records to one link: the share id, the share's slug, or the link itself.

continue_from.description: The `continue_from` value a previous answer gave selects the rows after it. Omission starts from the first row.

tools.name: replace_document
tools.description: Replaces the contents of a document already on HTMLRadar, which is how a page that has been sent is updated. Every existing link stays exactly as it is (same address, same settings, same reading history) and serves the new contents from the next time it is opened, so nobody is sent a second link; a link that is switched off or past its end date stays closed. The new HTML is screened for phishing signals as every upload is, and readers of a page the screen holds see that it is not available yet. The previous version stays listed in the document's version history on the website. There is no restore, from Claude or on the website; going back means replacing the contents again with the earlier page. Recipients may already have read the old contents. The call needs `expected_version`, the version get_document or list_documents shows, so a newer version is never overwritten. The tool accepts either the whole new page in `html`, up to 5 MB with its images as references, or `edits`: pieces of text to find in the page get_document returned, each with its replacement and each appearing exactly once. Past 5 MB, only `edits` work, because only the changes travel. A change to a page already on HTMLRadar is made by reading it with get_document and sending back the edited short form, or only the `edits`: that works for pages up to 30 MB, the same limit as the website, and keeps every image; a whole new file is needed only to replace the page itself. A page with more than 20 MB of text and code besides its images cannot be read or changed here, and a change that would take a page past that is refused, so nothing is stored. Images that need a login, expiring image addresses and local file paths do not load for readers of the link; an image embedded in the HTML as a data URI travels inside the page. The tool does not check that images load. On an update, embedded PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images appear as short htmlradar-image references in the document contents. Unchanged references restore the original images, so only new images count towards the 5 MB limit. Other embedded images, such as SVG, stay in the markup and count towards it.

announce.description: Whether readers see what changed and subscribers receive an alert. Omitted means an announcement only when every live link is company-only; otherwise the replacement is quiet.

note.description: Optional note for an announced update, at most 140 characters.

document_id.description: The document whose contents are being replaced. Every link to it keeps working.

html.description: The new HTML markup, in full. It may keep the htmlradar-image references get_document returned. Mutually exclusive with `edits`.

edits.description: Changes to the page get_document returned, applied in order. Each `find` must appear exactly once in the page at that point. Between 1 and 200. Mutually exclusive with `html`.

find.description: Text in the page or passages get_document returned, copied exactly; it must appear exactly once in the whole page.

replace.description: The text that takes its place.

expected_version.description: The document's current version as you last saw it: get_document and list_documents show it, and each replace_document result gives the new one. When the document has been replaced since, nothing is replaced and the call says so, so newer work is never overwritten.

request_id.description: Optional on a first attempt. When a previous call may have been applied, the request_id named by its error makes a retry return the first result instead of doing it twice.

annotations.title: Replace a document, keeping every link

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Returns the current contents of a document on HTMLRadar so they can be changed and put back with replace_document. A change to a page already on HTMLRadar is made this way, for pages up to 30 MB, the same limit as the website: read the page here, then send the edited short form, or only the changes, to replace_document; a whole new file is needed only to replace the page itself. Each embedded PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP image appears as a short htmlradar-image reference instead of its data; unchanged references restore the original images, and other embedded images, such as SVG, stay in the markup. Up to 5 MB of text and code, with its images as references, the whole page comes back. Between 5 MB and 20 MB it is too large to return whole: pass `query`, a word or phrase from the part to change, and it returns up to 20 passages where that text appears, exact text for `edits`. Over 20 MB of text and code besides its images, the page cannot be read or changed here. A document served from its own address has no stored contents to return. It reads only this account's documents and changes nothing.

document_id.description: The document to read: the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

query.description: Text to find, 1 to 200 characters, matched literally with letter case ignored, such as a product name or a price. Returns up to 20 passages around the matches, and how many there are, instead of the whole page. For a page too large to read whole, the passages provide exact text for edits.

annotations.title: Read a document to change it

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Reports which HTMLRadar account the API key belongs to (its email address), the plan it is on and how many of its free tracked links it has used out of the free allowance, or that tracked links are unlimited. It also reports what this connection may do (read only, or read and publish), any notice about the plan, and any notice about a newer version of the HTMLRadar package.

annotations.title: Show the HTMLRadar plan and free links used

tools.name: get_page_guidelines
tools.description: Returns HTMLRadar's guidelines for pages that read well on phones and give accurate section reading times. It reads no account data and changes nothing.

instructions: HTMLRadar sends a web page, deck, report or dashboard to the specific people chosen for it, controls who can open it, shows how each person read it, and updates it on the same link. share_html publishes a page the user intends to send; get_share_activity reports how a link was read; list_shares finds a link from an earlier conversation, and list_documents a document that has no link yet; create_share makes another link for a document that already exists; get_document and replace_document read and replace a document's contents behind the links already sent, so every reader sees the new version on the same link; get_share and update_share read and change a sent link's settings (who can open it, the email gate and code, the password, the end date, the copy lock) without changing the link; revoke_share switches a link off, or back on; list_attachments, add_attachment and remove_attachment manage the files attached to a document; get_reading_records returns the reading records the website exports; get_page_guidelines returns how a page reads well on phones and gives accurate section reading. No tool deletes a page or a link; that is only on the website. On a free account, publishing spends one of two tracked links, whoami says how many are used, and a publish refused for that reason stays refused until the plan changes. A call that needs new permissions returns a link the user approves in one click, after which the connection continues. Publishing, replacing, changing a setting, adding or removing a file and switching a link off each change what a recipient sees or spend a link, and are done only when the user has asked for them.
